Hi Sofia —

Thanks for the fast follow-up. I accepted the demo invite this morning but my calendar is showing the start time as '09:00' with no zone (it reads as a local floating time). Our APAC team forwarded the invite from a colleague in Sydney, and when it arrived it converted to my Pacific calendar incorrectly. On my end that now shows as 09:00 PT, which would be 02:00 here — obviously not workable.

Can you confirm the intended time in UTC so I can lock it in and circulate to our regional leads?

Three windows that would work for us next week (all times local for me, PST):
- Tue 23 Feb, 08:00–08:45 PST
- Wed 24 Feb, 16:00–16:45 PST
- Thu 25 Feb, 01:00–01:45 PST (not ideal, open to swapping for the EU folks)

I've attached a screenshot showing the floating time label (attached: gcal-floating.png) — I can't tell whether the TZ field was stripped when the invite was forwarded.

Appreciate the help — happy to do whatever makes the calendar canonical (UTC/explicit TZ) so we avoid more confusion.

Best,
Elena

Hi Elena — thanks for the screenshot, that helps.

You're right — when an invite is forwarded from a calendar in a different region, Google sometimes drops the explicit TZ id and treats the start time as "floating," which then gets interpreted in the recipient's local zone. That would explain why a 09:00 slot in Sydney ended up as 09:00 local for you.

To avoid this, I can:
- Send a new invite with the time explicitly set in UTC (e.g., 2027-02-23T16:00Z) and an explicit TZ parameter in the iCalendar (.ics).
- Or create three separate invites for the slots you listed and label them with the UTC stamp so the forwarded copies don't rely on implicit conversions.

I've attached an .ics with the three candidate windows marked in UTC (demo-availability.ics). If any of those work, reply with the one you prefer and I will send an explicit, non-forwarded invite from our account so the TZ metadata is preserved.

Also looping Karthik and Marissa to confirm the preferred demo configuration and to make sure we have EU-friendly options for their leads. Dylan — flagging because we may want to include a fallback (lighter model) region for the slot if capacity is tight.

Thanks —
Sofia
Solutions Partner Manager | Redwood Inference

Hey all — quick note from the sales side: we should standardize on UTC for invites when prospects include multi-region teams.  It's the least surprising and avoids DST edge cases between US/EU/APAC.

Sofia — please pick the Tue 23 Feb slot at 16:00 UTC (that should map to Tue 08:00 PST for Elena and Wed 03:00 AEDT for Sydney — sorry APAC folks, that's the tradeoff). I'll update the HubSpot opportunity record: https://hubspot.example/record/HS-3492 (ACME-POC-2027).

If anyone expects an external forward, put this text into the invite body: "Time is specified in UTC (Z) to preserve region-agnostic scheduling; please do not forward without checking your calendar TZ settings." That has helped reduce false accepts for us in other deals.

-karthik
